description:
## What

`perform_request` and `perform_follow_redirect` both call `Crest::Request.execute`
with the same 7 kwargs. Extract a single `execute_crest(method, url, headers)`
helper inside `CrestHttpClient`.

## Source (from `src/fetcher/crest_http_client.cr`)

The two near-identical blocks are at roughly:

- Lines ~155–163 (in `perform_request`)
- Lines ~225–233 (in `perform_follow_redirect`)

Both do:
    Crest::Request.execute(
      method,
      url,
      headers: headers,
      max_redirects: 0,
      handle_errors: false,
      connect_timeout: @config.timeout.connect,
      read_timeout: @config.timeout.read,
      tls: build_tls_context
    )

## Why

- Classic DRY violation. Any change to the call shape (e.g. adding
  `write_timeout`, `user_agent`, default headers) has to be made in two places.
  Already a reliability risk: the two are easy to drift.

## How

Add a private helper:

    private def execute_crest(method : Symbol, url : String,
                              headers : ::HTTP::Headers | Hash(String, String)) : Crest::Response
      Crest::Request.execute(
        method, url,
        headers: headers,
        max_redirects: 0,
        handle_errors: false,
        connect_timeout: @config.timeout.connect,
        read_timeout: @config.timeout.read,
        tls: build_tls_context
      )
    end

Use it from both call sites.

## Constraints

- Header type differences: `perform_request` passes `crest_headers : Hash(String, String)`
  via `HeaderBuilder.build_for_crest`; `perform_follow_redirect` passes the same
  hash through. The helper accepts a union or just `Hash(String, String)` since
  that's what both callers actually pass.
- No behavior change.

## Done when

- Single source of truth for the Crest call in `crest_http_client.cr`.
- Specs pass.
